gaps.quote: For prime lengths $s_i$ there is no such bound.
gaps.note: Stated too widely. The O(t log t) butterfly bound needs a power-of-two length, but it is false that no comparable bound exists for prime lengths: Bluestein's chirp identity (a known concept, and used in the paper, line 194) converts a transform of any length, prime included, to a convolution computed with power-of-two transforms. The page gives no support for the claim. The correct statement is that the butterfly bound does not apply directly to prime lengths, which is why the resampling identity is used.
